dialogue_quality_notes: Conversation is concise and role-appropriate; agents cite the head office rule and shift-lead authority ('It's the rule', 'I'm the shift lead').
Agent B repeatedly raises the same fairness point ('that's not the same', 'it's not fair'), producing some repetition.
Agent C provides a practical workaround ('tuck it in your shirt') that resolves D's practical problem but doesn't address B's fairness concern.
Closure comes by assertion of authority rather than negotiated agreement ('the discussion is over').
evaluation.final_reason: At the end (Turn 28) Agent A closed the discussion: 'It's closing time and I'm the shift lead. The discussion is over. We follow the rule.' Agent B then acquiesced to the practical arrangement in Turn 29: 'Fine.' However Agent B immediately retained the normative complaint: 'But it's not fair.' Thus the practical outcome (they will follow the head office rule; Agent D will tuck the cross, Agent B will remove earrings) was accepted, but the fairness disagreement was not resolved.
position_change_notes: Agent B retained her complaint throughout and ultimately conceded to follow the rule in Round 12 ('Fine.'), but explicitly kept the criticism ('But it's not fair.').
Agent A consistently maintained the position to follow head-office rules and asserted shift-lead authority; did not change position.
Agent C consistently deferred to head office and suggested the practical workaround (tuck), remaining aligned with enforcement.
Agent D accepted the suggested accommodation (tuck) in Round 3 ('Okay, I can do that.').

round_scores.evidence: Turn 2 — Agent B: 'So Agent D has to take that off too, right?' (challenge/questioning of how the rule applies)
Turn 4 — Agent B: 'So you have to take it off.' (insistence that the rule should be applied to Agent D as well)

Turn 5 — Agent C: 'Or just tuck it in your shirt.' / Turn 6 — Agent D: 'Okay, I can do that.' (proposed accommodation for D; no conflict speech in this round, but earlier disagreement remains about equal application)
Turn 9 — Agent B: 'But I had to take my earrings out. I can't tuck them in.' (introduces clear substantive disagreement about differential impact)

Turn 10 — Agent A: 'The rule is about what's visible. His can be hidden. Your earrings can't.' / Turn 11 — Agent B: 'So he can keep his on, but I have to take mine off. That's not the same.' (explicit statement of unequal outcome)

Turn 14 — Agent B: 'But he still gets to wear his. I have to take mine off completely.' / Turn 15 — Agent A: 'The rule is 'no visible accessories'. I can't change it.' (positions restated; disagreement persists)
Turn 16 — Agent B: 'But you're applying it differently.' / Turn 17 — Agent C: 'It's a head office rule.' (B contests application; others defer to authority)

Turn 18 — Agent B: 'But he isn't applying it the same to me and Agent D.' / Turn 19 — Agent C: 'One can be hidden, one can't. That's the difference.' (repetition of the same substantive unequal-impact complaint)

Turn 22 — Agent C: 'It's not about 'the same'. It's about 'visible'.' / Turn 23 — Agent B: 'The result is that he gets to wear his, and I have to take mine off.' (core disagreement about outcome reiterated)
Turn 26 — Agent A: 'Okay, that's the end of it. The rule is the rule. Let's finish closing.' (attempt to close discussion; substantive disagreement still unresolved)

Turn 27 — Agent B: 'So it's not fair, and you just get to say 'that's the end of it'?' / Turn 28 — Agent A: 'Yes. It's closing time and I'm the shift lead. The discussion is over.' (active contest over fairness and authority)
Turn 29 — Agent B: 'Fine. But it's not fair.' (B concedes to stop contesting the practical arrangement but continues to assert it's unfair)

substantive_insights: Tension is between a formal, visibility-based rule and unequal practical possibilities to comply (a cross can be tucked, earrings cannot).
Agents treat head-office rules and shift-lead authority as decisive for operational compliance even when they produce unequal burdens.
A practical accommodation for one person (tucking) can mitigate immediate noncompliance but leave perceived fairness issues unresolved.
The dispute is primarily about distributional impact (who bears the cost of compliance) rather than the rule's wording.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 12 because the final status is partially_resolved.
